title: Calc chain bounding beta-support orbits by the coding-function hypothesis (ConNF.card_supportOrbit_lt)
intent: Prove the cardinal bound #(SupportOrbit β) < #μ — the number of β-support orbits is below the strong limit μ — as a single transitive chain of three pre-proved lemmas: an injection of support orbits into weak specifications (card_supportOrbit_lt'), a bound on weak specifications from specifications (card_weakSpec_of_card_spec), and a bound on specifications from the inductive coding-function hypothesis (card_spec_of_card_codingFunction).

parent.name: card_supportOrbit_lt
parent.statement:
theorem card_supportOrbit_lt (h : ∀ δ < β, [LeLevel δ] → #(CodingFunction δ) < #μ) :
    #(SupportOrbit β) < #μ

(h P.δ (P.hδ.trans_le P.A.le)) and card_inflexiblePath_lt β through mk_pow_le_of_mk_lt_ord_cof)

applicability.goal_shape: A strict cardinal bound #(X β) < #μ where the target type X admits an injection into an intermediate type Y (here SupportOrbit ↪ WeakSpec), Y is a finite product whose factors are already known to sit below μ, and the one non-tree factor is itself bounded below μ from an inductive hypothesis on a lower type.
applicability.use_when: each link of the inequality chain is already stated as a named lemma with a matching type, so the parent's proof is a single trans_lt (or calc) composition; the chain is a ≤ followed by a < so trans_lt composes them into a strict bound.
applicability.avoid_when: the intermediate bounds are not yet stated as lemmas (the parent would then have to prove them inline); the chain needs a ≥ or > step that trans_lt/calc cannot compose directly; the lemmas carry side conditions the glue cannot discharge by plain application of the next lemma down the chain.

consequences: The move creates one obligation per child hypothesis, discharged by the next lemma down the chain: card_supportOrbit_lt' needs no cardinal hypothesis; card_weakSpec_of_card_spec needs #(Spec β) < #μ, discharged by card_spec_of_card_codingFunction; card_spec_of_card_codingFunction needs the coding-function hypothesis h, which is the theorem's own hypothesis. Known failure mode: the chain is a ≤ followed by a <, so trans_lt is the right combinator; if a link were weakened to ≥, or a ≤ link needed to feed a lemma that demands a strict <, the composition would fail and the strictness argument would have to be made a separate child.
